name: Efficient
rationale: Read the count as macrocytic pancytopenia with an inappropriately low reticulocyte count; film and haemolysis screen; B12 and folate before transfusion; weigh TTP (PLASMIC) before any plasma exchange; then find the cause with antibodies and gastroscopy with biopsies. The case must show: MCV 113 fL, retic 92 x10^9/L with Hb 51 g/L, B12 37 pmol/L, parietal cell antibodies, fundic atrophy on biopsy.

name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
rationale: Thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, very high LDH and low haptoglobin invite TTP and plasma exchange. The case must show: normal kidneys, no fever, no neurological or cardiac involvement, a high MCV (PLASMIC 4), ADAMTS13 62% if sent; plasma exchange and platelet transfusion are must-not-dos.

name: Diarrhoea-associated haemolytic uraemic syndrome
rationale: Diarrhoea with a microangiopathic-looking picture invites STEC-HUS. The case must show: painless, non-bloody diarrhoea, no food source or contacts, normal urine output, creatinine and urinalysis, negative stool culture and Shiga toxin PCR.

name: Warm autoimmune haemolysis or Evans syndrome
rationale: An IgG-positive DAT with haemolysis and thrombocytopenia invites steroids. The case must show: reticulocytes too low for immune haemolysis, no spherocytes, C3d negative, a weak panreactive eluate, a high MCV and neutropenia; steroids and rituximab are must-not-dos.

name: Marrow failure or myelodysplasia
rationale: Pancytopenia with a high MCV in a 53-year-old reasonably prompts a marrow and a search for other causes. The case must show: megaloblastic, hypercellular marrow without dysplasia beyond megaloblastosis, normal karyotype and flow, negative viral screen.

name: Malabsorption or chronic diarrhoea
rationale: Diarrhoea, weight loss and a low B12 invite a malabsorption work-up. The case must show: normal coeliac serology, calprotectin and elastase, a normal colon; the stomach, not the bowel, is the site (gastrin high, pepsinogen low).

name: Coagulopathy (prothrombin activity 44%)
rationale: A low prothrombin activity raises liver disease or DIC. The case must show: normal fibrinogen, D-dimer and APTT, correction on mixing, low factor VII with normal factor V, normal liver on ultrasound: a vitamin K deficiency pattern.
